## composables/useNearScreen

Which rows of a long list are on the screen or close to it,
so only those are drawn in full.

A list of several hundred cards takes most of a second to build, and is
built again each time it is shown. Its holder draws a row in full only
while `isNear` says so and leaves a blank of the row's height otherwise,
putting `vNear` on both with the row's key, so the list scrolls, and is
as long, as if every row were there.

Where the browser can't say (no IntersectionObserver), every row is near.

## useNearScreen

- `options` **[Object][2597]?** (optional, default `{}`)
  - `options.margin` **[number][2595]?** How far past the box's top and bottom
    still counts as near, in pixels (optional, default `400`)
  - `options.root` &#x20;

## near

The keys of the rows near the screen.

## composables/useNearTurns

Which of a chat's turns are in the page.

A long chat mounted whole costs what all of it costs. One of 781 messages came
to over eight thousand components and a few hundred megabytes, for a panel
that shows three or four turns at a time. So a turn is mounted only while it
is near: within a screen of what can be seen, either way. Further off it
stands as an empty block at the height it last had, so the scroll is as long
as it would be and nothing moves when a turn comes or goes.

A turn that has not been near yet stands at a guess, so that the scrollbar
says where in the chat the writer is before they have been through it: the
lines its text takes at the column's width, at the height a line comes to in
the turns measured so far, over what a turn takes besides its text. Against
a long chat at two widths, guessed from the newest few turns, the whole came
within a few percent; a flat guess was three quarters short. When a guess
above what is on screen is replaced by the real thing, or the guesses change,
the turn the writer is reading is put back where it was. Chromium does that itself, as scroll anchoring. WebKit anchors when
something above changes size but not when something is put into it, which is
what mounting a turn is, and without this the chat jumped on nearly every
step of scrolling up through a long one there.

Putting it back is moving the scroll position, except while a finger is on
the panel or it is still coasting from one. iOS stops a scroll dead when the
page moves it, so a long chat could not be flung through there: it stopped
at every turn that came in. Then the turns' container is shifted up or down
by its top margin instead, which WebKit leaves the scroll position alone for,
and once the panel has been still for a moment the shift is taken out and the
scroll position moved by as much, where moving it stops nothing.

Some turns stay whatever: the newest two, which are what was just sent and
the reply to it, where the writer is looking and where the chat takes them;
whatever the chat names in `keep`, such as a summary being written or the
turn a find is on; and a turn with an editor open in it, so that going to
look something up does not throw away what was being typed. Until the page has said which turns are
near, the newest few are mounted, so that a chat opens onto its end drawn.

A turn let go loses what its components held, so what the writer opened in
one — its reasoning, its tool calls, the raw text — is kept by the chat
instead, with `useTurnState`.

Without IntersectionObserver — under test — every turn is mounted.

## AHEAD

How far off screen a turn is mounted ahead of time: one screen either way.

Type: [string][2594]

## BASE_HEIGHT

What a turn takes besides its text: its header, its padding and border.

Type: [number][2595]

## UNKNOWN_WIDTH

## composables/usePictures

What a picture's path in a document is, and opening one.

A path is one of a document's own pictures (`.images/<id>/<name>`, see
`utils/pictures.js`), a link to a file document that is a picture, or an
address on the web. The editor draws what this says (`editor/pictures.js`),
and opens one: a picture at its own size in the viewer, an address outside
the app as a link's is. A picture pasted, dropped or inserted becomes the
document's own here (`take`), and so does one copied from another
document (`adopt`), so that each document keeps its own whatever becomes
of the other.

Design: `.llm/images_design.md`.

## utils/lineDiff

What changed between two versions of a text, line by line.

For showing a writer what a rewrite did, not for applying it: only the
lines that changed, in runs, each run the lines that went and the lines
that came in their place. A settled document differs from the one typed in
a bullet here and an escape there, and a run per place is what reads.

## LineChange

Type: [Object][2597]

### Properties

- `removed` **[Array][2596]<[string][2594]>** The lines that went, in order
- `added` **[Array][2596]<[string][2594]>** The lines in their place, in order

## MAX_MATCHED

Past this many lines on each side of the part that differs, the lines are
not matched up one by one: the table that matches them grows with the
square, and a change that big is one run anyway.

Type: [number][2595]

## changedLines

The runs of lines that differ between two texts.

The lines both share at either end are set aside first, which on a
rewrite of a few lines leaves little to match. What is left is matched by
the longest run of lines both keep in order, and every stretch between two
kept lines is a change.

### Parameters

- `before` **[string][2594]**&#x20;
- `after` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][2596]<[LineChange][2100]>** Empty when nothing changed

## composables/usePrint

A document printed, or saved as a PDF. Its page
(`files/printPage.js`) is put in the app's, and takes the app's place
while it prints.

Command-P prints the document open through the system's print dialog,
which saves a PDF too. Export as PDF… on a document's menu opens the same
dialog in a browser, and in the desktop app saves the PDF where the writer
says, without it.

The page stays until the print is done with it, so a browser that prints
after `print()` has returned, as Safari on a phone does, still has it. The
window's title is the document's meanwhile: the dialog names the PDF by it.

## composables/useProfiles

The chat profiles, built-in and the writer's own, as one list.

The built-ins lead, the way they did in the prompt library and for the same
reason: they are what a chat falls back to, and a list whose first entries
move as saved ones come and go is a list nobody can point at.

A built-in's wording cannot be edited. Saving a chat's settings to one makes
a copy of the writer's own, `Default - Custom`, and moves the chat onto it;
a copy of one of the writer's own is numbered, `Notes (2)`, as copies are
everywhere else. What a pick in a chat leaves on a profile, its model, its
effort, whether edits wait and its tools, is kept on a built-in all the
same, in the application state beside it (`builtInProfiles`), so it is
never copied for that.

Every profile has a preset its chats start on. One never picked on starts
them on the preset chats ran on before profiles kept their own, while it is
here, and otherwise on the built-in one.

An NSFW built-in and its general counterpart are one entry, which the
settings switch decides between. Off, the general one is offered, and a chat
or a project that names the NSFW one runs on the general one; on, the other
way round, so card chats, which start on Roleplay, start on Roleplay (NSFW).
Either way the chat keeps the id it names, and flipping the switch back puts
it where it was.

The roleplay built-ins are offered only while the Roleplay extension is on.
A chat or a project already on one runs on it all the same.

## composables/useProjectActions

What can be done to a project, as menu items: its settings, an
export, showing its folder, sharing it or keeping it on this device, and
removing it: to the trash, with an Undo, whether it is this account's or
shared with it. The outline's menus offer them for the project open, and a
list of projects for any of them, without opening it.

A project not open here has only its story and its root in memory. That is
enough to remove it or show its folder; what wants its documents reads them
first (`readWhole`). One open in another window is that window's, and only
its folder can be shown from here.

## keptOffSync

or by another device to itself and then brought back out of the trash here.

### Parameters

- `beforeDelete` **[Array][2596]<[Object][2597]>?** Items of the caller's to go above Remove

it all again, and the writer can ask again. One gone to another window

## composables/useProjects

Every project, and starting, importing, opening, trashing and
deleting them. A project's name, and when it was last edited, live on its root
document, so the list loads those alongside the story records — one keyed
read, not a tree per project.

In the desktop app a project is open in one window at a time
(`platform/windows.js`), and one open in another window is shown there.
The list is read again once another window or tab has changed it, when it
is next wanted.

### Examples

```javascript
const projects = useProjects()
await projects.init()
projects.open(projects.projects.value[0].id)
```

## composables/useProjectSearch

The writer's search across a project (`editor/projectSearch`):
what they look for and how, what it finds in the documents as they are now,
and going to one of the matches.

What was looked for is kept for each project while the app is open, since
the sidebar's list is made again each time it shows. What it finds follows
the documents: it is found again once the typing pauses, in the field or in
a document.

Going to a match is asked here and taken up by the view that shows its
document, as a comment is gone to (`useComments`): the editor, a plain
document's field and a file of code open their find on the query, on that
match; a PDF opens at the page the match is on. The going is made before
the document opens, so a view made for it finds it waiting, and is taken
once, so a tab come back to later stays where the writer left it.

Mod-Shift-F shows the list with the caret in its field, looking for what
is selected if that is a few words on one line.

- `at` **[number][2595]?** Where it is in the text, in a document found in

## composables/usePrompts

The system prompt library: the prompts that ship with the app
plus the ones the user has saved, in one list.

A chat points at one prompt and sends its text as it stands, the way it
runs on a profile's parameters as they stand: an edit reaches every chat on
that prompt, and a chat that wants different wording gets a copy. The
built-ins are read-only, so editing one is what makes that copy — see
`components/writer/chats/ChatSettings.vue`.

## composables/useSettingsFile

In the desktop app, the settings file a script left in the
app's data folder, imported as the app opens.

A team's script installs the app and leaves `inksprite-settings.json` in
its data folder: the connection to their model server, a preset on it,
their MCP servers. The app imports it before any store has read a row, so
nothing needs reloading, and without asking, since whoever left it there
meant it. Only what the file changed since it was last imported goes in,
so what the writer did since stands (`utils/settingsFile.js`). A file that
couldn't be read is said so once the app is up; one that went in is not.

Design: `.llm/settings_import_design.md`.

## importSettingsFile

Import the settings file a script left, if there is one. Called once, as
the app opens, before it mounts. Never throws: a file that can't be read
is said so once the app is up, and the app opens as it would without one.

Returns **[Promise][2599]\<void>**&#x20;

## useSettingsFileNotice

Say why the settings file couldn't be imported, once the app is up.
Called by the app, in its setup. It stays until it is closed: the file
stays broken until someone fixes it.

## composables/useSignIn

Connecting an account by signing in, with OAuth (PKCE), to a
service that makes the app a key for it: OpenRouter and NanoGPT
(`signIn` on their types, `ai/providers.js`).

`start` sends the writer to the service. In a browser that is a tab of its
own, which the service sends back to `/connect/<type>`
(`SignInCallback.vue`); that page calls `finish` and tells the tab that
started it with an `oauth-success` message. In the desktop window it is the
system browser, which comes back to the window's listener on localhost:
`start` calls `finish` itself and posts the same message to its own window.
Whoever listens for the message hears it either way.

The key goes on the connection signed in from, or on a new connection of
the service where there was none, which takes the built-in's id where the
service had one (`addConnection`).

## signInPath

Where a service sends the writer back after signing in.

### Parameters

- `type` **[string][2594]** The connection's type: `openrouter`, `nanogpt`

Returns **[string][2594]**&#x20;

## composables/useSkills

The writer's own skills: the library, and what the rest of the
app asks of it.

The rows are `stores/skillStore.js`; the skills made from them — the model's
tools, the writer's commands — are the registry in ai/skills, which the
store keeps up to date. This is what components and the turn reach for.

A skill's file is kept as it is typed, whatever state it is in
(`writeSkill`), and one that can't be used yet says why (`problemOf`) and
is offered to nobody. The name a skill is kept under is the last one its
file gave it that it could have: a name that is another skill's, a
command's or a tool's stays in the file and is not taken, so the skill that
had the name first keeps it. A skill brought in from outside is checked
before it is kept at all (`saveSkill`).

- `settings` &#x20;
- `from` &#x20;
- `to` &#x20;

## composables/useSpeech

Something read aloud then and there: a chat message, in one
voice. One thing at a time, app-wide — starting another stops the one that
was speaking, the way one person reads.

What is read comes as lines, a paragraph each. They are asked for in order,
each as soon as the last is back, and played in order, each as soon as it
is there: the reading starts when the first line arrives rather than when
the last does, and the next is usually waiting by the time one ends.
Nothing is kept; read again, it is asked for again.

A document's narration is a different thing (`useNarration`): many voices,
audio kept and joined into a track. This is for hearing a message once.

## composables/useSpelling

The editor's spelling, for a project: the checker set to the
writer's settings and told the words the project knows, and what the menu
on a flagged word does with a word or a lint.

A project knows the words in its own dictionary (`Story.spelling`) and the
names in its documents' titles, taken without asking: a character sheet
titled "Marisol Vey" teaches it both names. Only a word with a capital is
taken, so a title's ordinary words don't count. A typo in a title passes
too, which is the price.

A phone keeps its keyboard's checker for now, and so does a writer who
switched the app's checker off, or whose checker failed to start.

## composables/useToolApprovals

The tool calls waiting on the writer before they run.

A server's tool that does not say it only reads asks first: the turn shows
the call and waits for Allow, Always allow (the tool, or everything from the
server), or Deny. So does a page the model keeps in the project
(`save_web_page`), whose Always allow is for every page from then on. A
tool can also ask a question of its own as it runs, whose Always allow
the tool keeps: explore, saying what it would cost. The
wait belongs to the turn rather than to the tool, so it does not count
against the tool's time limit, and a turn that is stopped answers every
call it was waiting on with Deny.

Kept in memory, by call: a page reloaded mid-turn has lost the turn anyway.

## Decision

`always` is the tool from now on; `always-server` is everything the server
has.

Type: (`"allow"` | `"always"` | `"always-server"` | `"deny"`)

## composables/useToolChoices

Gives every profile and chat, once, the web, Python and MCP
servers as their own tools' switches (ai/tools/choice.js), from the lists
that said before: web search's profiles, Python's, and each server's, and
a chat's own choice of each where it made one. See `.llm/tools_design.md`.

Each says what is off, as the rest of a choice does. A group a profile or
chat had on stays on; one it had off is switched off; and in a profile that
offers only some groups (Roleplay, Blank), and the chats on it, one it had
on joins the ones it offers. Nothing is taken off, so a second device
giving the same chats the same lists changes nothing, and a device that
hasn't yet does no harm to what the first wrote.

A group that isn't there to be offered on this device is left alone, so
that, set up later, it is on wherever nothing said otherwise, as anything
added is: the web without a service chosen, and Python where it can't run.
The old fields and lists are left as they were, for an app from before.

## composables/useTopmostEscape

Escape closes the dialog on top, and only that one.

Every PrimeVue dialog listens for Escape on the document and closes itself
when it hears one, so a dialog opened over another — the provider
configuration over the settings, a confirmation over either — takes the
one beneath it down too. A dialog that uses this instead of its own
listener closes only when it is the topmost dialog on the page, and only
for an Escape pressed inside it.

The second half is for what opens over a dialog without a mask of its own:
a ⋮ menu, a popover, a select's list. PrimeVue puts those on the body,
outside the dialog, and they close themselves on the Escape pressed in
them before it reaches the document — so by the time it does, they are no
longer open to be asked about. Where the key was pressed still says whose
it was.

## MASK_SELECTOR

Every dialog mask on the page.

Type: [string][2594]

## isTopmostMask

Whether the mask given is on top: nothing has been opened over it. Each is
given a higher z-index than the last as it opens, which is what says.
Where it is on the page doesn't: a dialog's mask goes where the dialog was
first mounted, so the settings, mounted with the writer, come before a
dialog mounted later and opened under them. Of masks with one z-index, the
later on the page is on top.

### Parameters

- `mask` **([Element][2603] | null | [undefined][2602])**&#x20;

Returns **[boolean][2600]**&#x20;

## top

Type: ([Element][2603] | null)

## composables/useTreeDrop

Dropping a document on a folder's row, to put it in the folder.

The outline's rows are sorted by vuedraggable, which only knows lists: a
row dropped on another lands before or after it, in the list that row is
in, so a folder could only be gone into through the list under it — a strip
a few pixels high, and none at all while the folder is shut. So while a row
is being dragged, this watches where the pointer is. Over the middle of a
folder's row, that folder is where the drop goes: the row is marked, the
list is told to move nothing, and the drop moves the document in. Over the
top or bottom of a row, the list sorts as before. A shut folder held over
for a moment opens, so the drag can go on into it.

Wherever the drop would go, that folder is shown, its row and everything
in it, as VS Code shows it: the folder whose row the drag is over, or the
one whose list the row being dragged has been sorted into. The row being
dragged sits in that list where it would land, drawn at that folder's
depth rather than the one it came from (DocumentNode's style).

One drag happens at a time, so the state is the module's.

## EDGE

How much of a row, from the top and from the bottom, means before and after it.

Type: [number][2595]

## OPEN_AFTER

How long a shut folder is held over before it opens, in milliseconds.

Type: [number][2595]

## zoneOf

Where on a row a point is: its top or bottom edge, or its middle.

### Parameters

- `rect` **{top: [number][2595], height: [number][2595]}** The row's box
- `y` **[number][2595]** The point, in the same coordinates

Returns **(`"before"` | `"into"` | `"after"`)**&#x20;

##

Type: ([string][2594] | null)

##

Type: ([string][2594] | null)

## composables/useTreeHistory

Undo and redo for what the writer does in a project's
outline: making a document or a folder, renaming one, moving one, deleting
one.

Command-Z in the outline takes the last of these back, and Shift-Command-Z
does it again, as Finder does with files. Only what the writer does in the
outline is kept: what a model, an import or sync does to the tree is not
theirs to take back with a key, and the editor keeps the text's own
history.

A step is taken back only from where it left things. A document renamed,
moved or deleted since is not put back over what happened after: the step
is let go of, and the key does nothing. A delete is taken back out of the
trash, so a delete is kept only where deletes go there.

Taking back the making of a document deletes it, with whatever was written
in it since. It goes to the trash, and comes back out of it on a redo.

One history per project, for as long as the page is open.

## LIMIT

How many steps are kept to take back.

Type: [number][2595]

any, and a toast to restart into one; in a browser, a toast to reload into

## composables/useVersions

A text document's versions, as the Versions dialog shows
them: listed, compared with the text now, restored, named, kept and
deleted. Taking them is `stores/versionsStore.js`'s.

A restore is a change from outside the editor like any other: the text as
it stands is kept as a version first, so a restore is undone by restoring
that one. See `.llm/versions_design.md`.

## showing

## showing

The document whose versions are showing, from anywhere in the writer: the
outline's menu, a tab's. One for the app.

## picking

The version to show first, when the dialog was opened on one: the text
that lost a clash. Taken by the dialog once it has the list.

## useVersionsPanel

Where the Versions dialog is opened from, and closed.

## useVersions

### Parameters

- `storyId` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

## list

A document's versions, the newest first.

### Parameters

- `documentId` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][2599]<[Array][2596]\<Version>>**&#x20;

## keepNamed

Keep the text a document has now, under a name.

### Parameters

- `documentId` **[string][2594]**&#x20;
- `name` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][2599]<(Version | null)>**&#x20;

## composables/useWebSearch

Web search as the settings set it up: which service is in
use and whether a page is kept without asking, in Settings › Extensions,
and each service's key, in Settings › Connections. See web/ and
.llm/web_search_design.md.

Choosing a service checks it at once where that costs nothing (listing its
tools). Connect checks it with the key typed in, and where there is no free
check, as with Brave, does so with a search, the writer having asked.

## checks

## checks

## checks

## checks

What the last check of a service found, by service: answered, or why not.
App-wide, so the section shows it again when reopened.

## checking

The service being checked, while it is.

##

Type: (WebServiceId | null)

## PROBE

What Connect searches for, at a service with no free check.

Type: [string][2594]

## PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS

How long Connect waits for a search, in milliseconds.

Type: [number][2595]

## useWebSearch

## inUse

Whether a chat could search now, were it asked to.

## setKey

Keep a service's key. What a check of the last one found no longer holds.

### Parameters

- `id` **WebServiceId**&#x20;
- `key` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

## connect

Keep a service's key, and check it, with a search if need be.

### Parameters

- `id` **WebServiceId**&#x20;
- `key` **[string][2594]**&#x20;

## setAskBeforeSaving

Ask before the model keeps a page in the project, or stop asking.

### Parameters

- `ask` **[boolean][2600]**&#x20;
